transcript.text: And the third that very few people are talking about, but is probably one of biggest arbitrage opportunities because of how good the models are now, is to instead of building out the thing, build the factory for.

What do you mean by that? So let's say you want a product and we just released there something called AI First Index I run with all my Fortune 500 clients where interview their executives evaluate how AI first they are across like 16 different dimensions. And we decided through a combination of humans and AI to create a product for the public to be able to benchmark themselves on how AI first they are as individuals.

In that process I could have done one of two things. I could have gone Claude Code or Codex. Could've said hey interview me, get my AI First Index reports that I've used with previous clients, find every single workshop I have ever done with clients, build out the product, and then we iterate for several hours days until something is perfect and we release it. That is option one.

Option two is realizing that's probably not going to be the only product you build. It's like what dev tool companies did for engineering but you're creating dev tools that level for yourself. You are going to the kernel level. Instead of just building that product we instead built out a mini and very beginner software factory where we were building primitives like obviously we have to deal with login obviously we have to deal with payments.
